races.name: Twilight Racing On The Dee Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Country Park
runners_data.note: Rated 118 and a winner over 20f on good ground, this hold-up operator needs the pace to be genuinely searching to deploy his finishing effort — in a race Jiair Madrik is likely to control from the front at a steady tempo, Country Park's rearward position maps poorly to the likely race shape; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will have limited options without a target to reel in.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out following a win two starts back, Country Park arrives here in solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going, making him a leading player on 168 lb; 44 days off is the only query.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who has been freshened up after just 10 days between runs, Lermoos Legend's best form in similar going (2W6P) gives modest encouragement but his hold-up style leaves him equally dependent on a stronger pace than this field is likely to generate; the tongue-tie and pads suggest connections are trying to sharpen his response.
runners_data.comment: Lermoos Legend arrives in sharp order on a ten-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going and a second last time out keeping connections buoyant; yet to win in his last five starts, and 163 lb is the weight he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Three from three in his most recent outings, all at around 20-21f on good ground, this seven-year-old front-runner could not be better positioned to exploit a lone lead — Theo Gillard simply needs to find a rhythm and let him jump; the headgear (hood/tongue-tie) is unchanged and the 63-day break is the only mild query.
runners_data.comment: Jiair Madrik has won three of his last five starts in recent form, including three consecutive victories, and has experience of today's distance and going, but he ranks last on our figures among these five and faces a stiff task off 160 lb after 63 days away.

runners_data.name: Duel Au Soleil
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's six-year-old carries the highest similar-going strike-rate among the rivals (1W5P in 12 runs) and his prominent style means he will sit ideally positioned just off Jiair Madrik throughout — he is the most natural beneficiary if anything goes wrong with the leader and represents the main threat on pure race-shape grounds.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat but clearly threatening, Duel Au Soleil brings strong placed form — second last time out and third three starts back — with experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Disco Davis
runners_data.note: Two pulled-up runs punctuate recent form and a trainer who is 0W from 3 in the 14-day window gives limited confidence, though Disco Davis has placed in similar distance-and-going conditions before; his prominent style keeps him involved early but the form figures of P4-3P6 suggest he needs things to fall right rather than manufacturing his own result.
runners_data.comment: Disco Davis shaped with promise when third three starts back and has experience of today's trip and ground, with our rating of 115 suggesting he holds strong claims; yet to win in recent starts and a 69-day absence leaves fitness the obvious query.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival inclined to challenge for the lead, he will dictate from the outset at whatever tempo suits Donald McCain's consistent front-runner. Duel Au Soleil and Disco Davis will push forward to prominent positions but neither carries the lead-at-all-costs profile needed to pressurise Jiair Madrik through the early stages of this 2m4½f trip on good ground. The two hold-up horses, Country Park and Lermoos Legend, will settle at the rear and depend entirely on Jiair Madrik either tying up or making jumping errors to deliver a late opportunity — on current evidence neither seems likely. This shape overwhelmingly favours the front-runner and prominent types who can track the controlled pace and produce a measured, jumping-clean finish, rather than hold-up performers who need a strongly-run race to land a telling late blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jiair Madrik Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik jumps cleanly, dictates an unhurried gallop and faces no sustained pressure from the prominent runners.
scenarios.body: McCain's horse, in the form of his life with three consecutive wins, is handed a solo lead and simply needs to jump and travel — the good ground and manageable distance suit his recent profile perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Duel Au Soleil or Disco Davis press Jiair Madrik consistently from the second fence and drain his stamina reserve approaching the final circuit.
scenarios.body: A contested pace lifts the tempo enough to stop Jiair Madrik quickening at his fences late on, giving the prominent types who tracked him the momentum to pass a flattening leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop On Tired Front-Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik sets a genuinely fast pace on his seasonal return from 63 days off and finds the trip stretching his stamina on the final climb.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly strong gallop burns off the prominent runners too, leaving Country Park and Lermoos Legend to mow down a tiring field with late reserves — though both need the leader to have gone very hard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Reshape Race
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik makes a costly mistake mid-race that halts his momentum and promotes the prominent pair into contention ahead of schedule.
scenarios.body: Duel Au Soleil, with the cleanest recent jumping profile in the field, is best placed to capitalise on a scrambled order; Disco Davis could also steal into contention before the two-out flight.

watchPoints.text: Jiair Madrik's jumping must be monitored from fence one — three consecutive wins mask a chase record that includes a fall and unseated rider earlier in his career, and a single bad error at pace could completely unravel the dominant race narrative.

Duel Au Soleil's proximity to Jiair Madrik throughout will be the key secondary story; if Ben Jones elects to sit upsides rather than just behind, he could inadvertently inject enough pressure to compromise both horses' jumping rhythm.

Country Park has a recent fall in his form (F) and arrives 44 days between runs — watch for any signs of jumping hesitancy early that would further compromise his ability to make ground from the rear.

Lermoos Legend's 10-day turnaround is unusually quick for an 11-year-old jumping horse — watch his movement in the parade ring for any sign of stiffness that could affect his willingness to attack fences.

With only five runners and Jiair Madrik effectively handed the race on a plate, watch for the field to become very strung out by halfway — any horse that loses its position at the fourth or fifth fence may find the gaps too large to close on good ground over this trip.

races.name: John Hewitt Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Roadlesstravelled
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner on OR 132 and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the ride, but recent form includes two pulled-ups (111PP/) and an 80-day absence which raises fitness questions despite the strong Good-ground sim record; front-running intent is certain and his class alone could carry him clear if sharper than his layoff suggests.
runners_data.comment: Roadlesstravelled showed a sharp winning streak with three victories in his last five starts, and he has experience of today's distance and going to call upon; the two subsequent pull-ups are a concern, but at 164 lb he remains our top-rated runner returning after 80 days off.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent on Good ground (13 from 15 sim-going attempts, five wins), wearing a tongue-tie, fresh from a win 19 days ago at OR 131, and Sean Quinlan is perfectly placed to exploit a prominent-but-controlled position as the front-runners battle each other into submission ahead.
runners_data.comment: Captain Cool arrives here in fine fettle, a winner last time out and victorious three starts back, with experience of both today's trip and conditions; the weight burden of 163 lb is the one factor he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton pushes him forward as standard — his style is confirmed lead — and all five recent runs have come on Good ground at 16f–22f, giving strong stamina and going confidence; OR of 115 leaves him at a class disadvantage but the Skelton yard's 7/20 T14 strike-rate and his placing consistency (4 from last 5 finishes) keep him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Consistent, with four top-four finishes in his last five, Krak arrives in fine fettle 19 days on, has run over today's trip and going, and his trainer is firing at 35% — yet he remains winless in recent starts, and 147 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: A 70-day absence following a run that ended in a pulled-up (49-P23) is a notable concern, and trainer Sarah-Jayne Davies' T14 record of 0/3 offers little encouragement; she races forward like the other two pace-setters and will be immediately involved in the early battle, so fitness rather than style is the decisive question here.
runners_data.comment: Ice In The Veins shaped with real promise when third last time out and second two starts back, suggesting he's knocking hard on the door, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; the main concern is that pull-up three starts back clouds his consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Roadlesstravelled, Krak, and Ice In The Veins are all confirmed front-runners in a field of just four, meaning the pace battle for the lead will be immediate and unrelenting from the off over 2m1½f on Good ground at Bangor. With three horses wired to go forward and only Captain Cool content to race prominently from a slightly more controlled position, the early stages are almost certain to produce a fast, honest gallop that tests stamina rather than sprint finish. The front-runners will likely string each other out, burning energy through multiple fences, and whoever blinks first or makes a jumping error is likely to capitulate quickly on a flat Bangor track that offers little recovery room. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead horse with superior stamina, jumping accuracy, and the class to sustain its effort — or a prominent-style horse patient enough to track the carnage and pounce in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Flame Out
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Roadlesstravelled, Krak, and Ice In The Veins produces a strong enough early gallop to exhaust each other before the final turn.
scenarios.body: Captain Cool, tracking the melee with Sean Quinlan's tactical savvy, is ideally placed to inherit the lead when the pace-setters tire, and his remarkable Good-ground record (13 places from 15 attempts) underlines that this surface suits him perfectly at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely Roadlesstravelled — asserts enough class advantage to establish a lead and repel rivals rather than burning out in a scrap.
scenarios.body: Roadlesstravelled's OR of 132, recent winning form, and Good-going sim record (3 placings from 9 at this going type) give him the profile to convert front-running dominance into a wire-to-wire success if the others fail to match his early stride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Krak Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Krak — sent forward as usual by Harry Skelton — gradually asserts from Bangor's final fence as others weaken, rewarding the Skelton yard's patient approach after their strong T14 strike rate of 7/20.
scenarios.body: Krak's Good-ground consistency (9 from 13 appearances) and distance profile covering 16f–22f suggest stamina is no issue, though his OR of 115 and lack of a recent win are concerns against higher-rated rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ice In The Veins Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Ice In The Veins, freshened after 70 days off, travels more powerfully than her OR of 113 suggests and times her run to beat tiring rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: She has placed third or better in several recent Good-ground efforts (10 from 12 sim-going placings), but trainer Sarah-Jayne Davies has zero wins from 3 runners in the last 14 days and James Best faces stiff opposition in the saddle.

watchPoints.text: Roadlesstravelled's two recent pulled-ups (PP in form) alongside an 80-day absence means his jumping may be rusty at the very moment he is being asked to front-run — watch for an early jumping error under Jonjo O'Neill Jr. that could unsettle the whole race.

Three confirmed front-runners (Roadlesstravelled, Krak, Ice In The Veins) going head-to-head over the opening fences creates a real risk of a race-changing incident at an early obstacle — a pile-up or loose horse could drastically reshape the entire contest.

Captain Cool's tongue-tie is listed (hg:tp) — worth monitoring in the pre-parade ring to confirm it is fitted correctly, as any distress could compromise his usually reliable jumping and prominent positioning for Sean Quinlan.

Ice In The Veins returns after 70 days off for a trainer whose recent form is 0 from 3 — if she jumps slowly or loses her pitch early, the three-way pace battle could leave her immediately detached and out of contention despite her reasonable sim-going record.

Bangor's flat, right-handed track with tight turns tends to favour horses who can settle into a rhythm and jump fluently rather than those burning energy fighting for position — watch which of the three front-runners is most composed through the first three fences as a guide to who will last home.

races.name: Paul Ferguson's Jumpers To Follow Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Cadillac Ranch
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won on Good 11 days ago and is likely to contest the early lead with Hidden Fortune; Miss Ellie Callwood's 7lb claim reduces the weight burden, and identical going conditions suit — the key question is whether a battle up front saps its reserves before the last.|

runners_data.name: Provision
runners_data.note: Recent winner at the track on Good ground with solid placing form in similar conditions, Provision's natural style is hold-up but the field's pace density means it will be unable to get far back — Barry Brennan's T14 strike rate of 1/3 in the last fortnight is modest, and 48 days off adds mild freshness doubt despite the strong form.|

runners_data.name: Hidden Fortune
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's confirmed front-runner has not run for 117 days, which is the standout fitness query here; Harry Skelton takes the mount which always signals intent, and two placing runs in similar going suggest the conditions are right — it just needs to be fit enough to sustain the lead after an inevitable early battle with Cadillac Ranch.|

runners_data.name: Pretty Darn Quick
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish flag and has shown nothing better than a seventh in five hurdle starts; its true hold-up style is squeezed by a field with multiple front-runners meaning it cannot get its preferred race, and an OR of just 73 makes it a significant handicap outsider even in a novice context.|

runners_data.name: Ride Like A Girl
runners_data.note: Has won on Good ground over 16f twice and brings a clean record across six starts on identical going at this level; Gavin Sheehan provides the most seasoned jockey-trainer combination for the scenario, and a prominent style that naturally settles just behind the two leaders is perfectly suited to a truly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Making a significant trip increase from 10-12f on the Flat to 2m½f over hurdles, and Donald McCain's T14 figure of 0/13 is a cold stat worth noting; showed decent pace on Good ground in flat races but the stamina query over this trip in a genuinely contested novice hurdle is real and headgear worn previously suggests a profile to watch rather than assume.|

runners_data.name: Rose Warrior
runners_data.note: A single hurdle run — eighth of 10 at a mile-long trip on Good — gives almost nothing to work with, and the hold-up style combined with a fades-in-finish flag makes it hard to construct a winning scenario; Ian Power picks up the ride, pony headgear is noted, and 63 days between runs adds further uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Evenly
runners_data.note: Two runs showing 11th and 6th on Good ground provide the thinnest form profile in the field; Brian Hughes is the most experienced jockey here and Donald McCain's second runner, but with no win or place on the board and only 147lbs carried, the form simply does not support optimism against front-runners this competitive.|

races.paceDynamic: Cadillac Ranch and Hidden Fortune are both confirmed front-runners, and with neither likely to concede the lead willingly, this 2m½f novice hurdle at Bangor will be run at an honest, competitive gallop from the outset rather than the false crawl that often distorts novice events. Cadillac Ranch arrives on an 11-day turnaround with recent winning form and a willing front-running profile; Hidden Fortune brings Dan Skelton's operation behind it and a similar desire to dictate, so early friction between the two is the defining structural feature of this race. That sustained gallop plays directly into the hands of prominent hold-up types who can settle within striking distance and pounce in the straight — particularly Ride Like A Girl and Secret Beach, who race prominently and have the going form on turf to capitalise. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Provision and Pretty Darn Quick are genuine hold-up types but are shown in midfield because the race shape forces them forward — of the two, Provision's better form figures make it the more likely to secure a workable position, though neither will get the true rear-to-rail run their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Cuts Each Other
scenarios.trigger: If Hidden Fortune and Cadillac Ranch lock horns up front and set a genuinely searching gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off, leaving the race wide open for those who tracked the pace in second rank and are still travelling at the business end; a true gallop at Bangor over this trip tends to thin the field decisively from three out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Gets Easy Toe
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Cadillac Ranch — establishes a clear lead without serious pressure and controls the tempo.
scenarios.body: With a single pace-setter dictating an honest but manageable gallop, the leader conserves enough for the finish and rivals chasing from behind find the winner always holding them; Cadillac Ranch's recent win on similar Good ground and experienced claims from Harry Skelton on Hidden Fortune both fit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between the two leaders is brief and the pace settles into something manageable, allowing prominent-racing horses to control their energy.
scenarios.body: Secret Beach, stepping up notably in trip from flat-bred roots, and Ride Like A Girl — who has won on identical Good ground over this course distance — both sit within two lengths of the pace and benefit from a rhythm that rewards their jumping fluency without the sprint test that a crawl would impose.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly extreme and the race reduces to a test of pure stamina from the home straight.
scenarios.body: Provision holds the best recent form figures of the hold-up brigade and, despite being pushed out of its natural position, possesses the class to make a late run if the front rank capitulates; Pretty Darn Quick has a fade-in-finish flag and Rose Warrior's single hurdles run was modest, making this scenario structurally fragile.

watchPoints.text: Hidden Fortune has not run for 117 days — watch its condition in the paddock and how quickly Harry Skelton sends it to the front; if it looks underdone, Cadillac Ranch may control the race uncontested.

Cadillac Ranch vs Hidden Fortune — if the two leaders are separated by less than a length at the first flight and neither gives way, the pace could become genuinely gruelling and open the race wide for Ride Like A Girl and Provision sweeping through.

Provision cannot get its natural hold-up position in this race shape — watch where Isabelle Ryder actually places it in the first half-mile; if it is trapped in midfield traffic rather than a clear back position, its finishing run will be compromised.

Secret Beach faces a substantial trip increase from Flat form at 10-12f — watch how it jumps the early flights, as any hesitation or novice jumping errors at this longer trip on a turning track could cost it vital lengths.

Pretty Darn Quick's fades-in-finish flag combined with its lowest-in-field OR of 73 makes it a potential hazard horse rather than a contender — watch it does not interfere with others if it weakens approaching the straight.|

races.name: Wrexham Lager Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Who's Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Donald McCain whose five-run form string includes a win and placed efforts on good ground, but sim-going figures are modest (0W1P from 4) and 91 days off the track is a notable freshness question; needs the pace to truly collapse to get competitive from the back.
runners_data.comment: Placed three times in his last five starts, Who's Glen has strong claims on a rating of 115 — the highest-ranked of the seven runners — and has run over today's trip and going before; the 91-day absence is the one query, though he arrives with a solid recent profile.

runners_data.name: Person of Interest
runners_data.note: Strong recent profile (2W5P across 14 good-ground runs) and Harry Cobden's booking is significant; last run just 11 days ago shows he stays in training well, and he has won at 16f on good, though stepping back up to 19f here asks whether his finishing kick arrives early enough.
runners_data.comment: Person of Interest arrives here just 11 days after a second-place finish, showing he is in good heart and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that pulled-up effort on his most recent start leaves a fitness question to answer.

runners_data.name: Rock Hurley
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing tongue-tie and a hood, won over 23f at this course on good ground and is the most credentialed leader in this field; amateur rider Mr Harry Brown takes a 10lb claim which helps the weight, though his last two runs after that win were modest (4th, 0th).
runners_data.comment: Rock Hurley won two starts back but has been unplaced on his latest outing, and 46 days off the track is a query; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 165 lb burden is no help to his chances.

runners_data.name: Lunar Orbit
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old has solid form on soft ground (0W4P from 6 good-ground runs suggests the faster surface is untested territory for this horse) and Harry Skelton is a significant booking; genuinely a hold-up horse by nature who is mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is congested — treat the shown position with caution.
runners_data.comment: Lunar Orbit arrives here on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, just 17 days ago, and has winning form in recent starts to his name; he handles today's going, his trainer is firing at 35% over the past fortnight, and a rating of 105 makes him a leading threat — the main concern is the 164 lb he shoulders.

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Donald McCain with a remarkable consistency record (2W7P from 12 qualifying runs) and ran just 10 days ago, suggesting he is fit and in a productive patch; prominent style suits this shape well and his multiple placed efforts at 17f on good make the trip and conditions ideal.
runners_data.comment: Zamond has winning form in recent starts and returns on a quick turnaround of ten days having run over today's trip and going, yet ranked sixth of seven on our figures he looks hard to fancy at these weights carrying 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Nathan Moscrop takes the ride on Brian Ellison's eight-year-old, who has two wins and six places in 11 qualifying runs but is by nature a hold-up horse compressed into a midfield slot by a crowded rear — his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.94 reflects meaningful displacement, and his best efforts tend to come in smaller, more galloping fields.
runners_data.comment: Dream Jet brings strong credentials here, having run over today's trip and going before, and his second last time out — backed by a rating of 105 — marks him as a genuine threat fresh off a 14-day break; the concern is a trainer operating at just 3% recently, and he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Auntie Maggie
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Alastair Ralph who will press Rock Hurley from the gate over a longer trip than her habitual 16f course outings; her record shows she often finds one or two too good (4th, 2nd, 5th, 3rd in recent outings), and the step up to 19f is an open stamina question that matters if she sets a strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Auntie Maggie is hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going; a pulled-up run two starts back and 153 lb to carry compound the concern, though a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for Greenall & Guerriero who ran just four days ago and has no win or place on record across her four qualifying good-ground starts; naturally a hold-up horse pushed toward midfield on the map, her STYLE_FIT displacement and raw figures make her the most vulnerable runner in this field on current evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m3½f trip on good ground at Bangor, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a saunter. Rock Hurley has won from the front at this track and trip, while Auntie Maggie will press hard, meaning the pace should be honest throughout with no let-up for those chasing. Zamond sits just off the pace in a prominent position and will be well-placed behind the duelling leaders, while Who's Glen and Person of Interest must close from further back in what shapes as a stamina-test finish. This contested, honest pace profile most favours prominent-to-mid-pack closers with proven stamina who can travel smoothly before delivering their effort in the final half-mile — pure hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged here because the field carries more hold-up types (Lunar Orbit, Dream Jet, Cappa Lass) than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning Zamond and the genuine hold-up duo with the best form are the most likely beneficiaries if the front-runners exhaust each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Fade, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie press each other hard enough to leave both weakened in the final two flights, allowing the first-wave chasers to mow them down.
scenarios.body: The honest duel between the two leaders sets a sustained gallop that burns through the field, and the first horse to arrive with a clean run off the pace claims it; Zamond, tracking in a perfect prominent position, is ideally placed to capitalise, while Person of Interest's strong recent going record makes him a genuine finisher if given a clear passage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Player Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Rock Hurley) establishes a clear rhythm and the other capitulates early, allowing a controlled pace that suits a prominent settler.
scenarios.body: Rock Hurley, the more experienced front-runner at this course and distance with a recent win over 23f on good ground, could find the race falling apart behind him if Auntie Maggie fades after setting the early tempo; Zamond pressing into a close second would then need to quicken, while the hold-up brigade face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly punishing and the leaders and prominent horses all empty out late, leaving the field strung out for a late closer to pick through.
scenarios.body: Person of Interest, with the strongest recent form record in similar going (2W5P in 14 qualifying runs) and Harry Cobden in the saddle, has the quality to thread through if there is carnage ahead; Who's Glen also has the profile to finish off a strongly-run race, though both must overcome being out of the natural hold-up territory this shape should create.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners reach an early truce and the gallop settles into a sedate rhythm that negates the closers entirely.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race rewards whoever sits handiest with the most energy in reserve through the final turn; Auntie Maggie's course-distance profile at shorter trips makes this a stretch, but Zamond's consistent placed record in measured-pace races gives him a second path to victory if the race crawls before quickening late.

watchPoints.text: Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie: if both refuse to concede the lead early, the pace could become unusually strong for good ground and dramatically shorten the race for closers — watch the first two furlongs to see which one blinks first.

Zamond: ran only 10 days ago and must bounce back quickly; if he shows any sign of flatness tracking the leaders into the back straight, his prominent position becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Lunar Orbit: Harry Skelton's booking suggests connections expect a big run, but the horse is a genuine hold-up type racing out of his natural position — watch whether Skelton attempts to drop him back from the mapped midfield slot once the tape rises.

Person of Interest: last seen running on just 11 days ago after a below-par effort (P finish); Harry Cobden's presence is a clear upgrade signal, but watch whether Cobden settles him patiently or attempts to improve position early in a race already loaded with pace.

Cappa Lass: having run four days ago and carrying the lowest weight in the field, watch her closely at the start — if she jumps poorly or is immediately detached, Toby Wynne's options are severely limited in a race where the pace will already be set.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds' five-year-old carries top weight and has won over this trip on Good ground, but her natural hold-up style is squeezed in a six-runner field where the pace is expected to be controlled — the compact field limits the finishing berths available late.|
runners_data.comment: Hello Sweety shaped well when third last time out, and a winner three starts back, giving her a lively recent profile that makes her a clear threat here; the main question is whether 52 days off the track has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Eremenko
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's confirmed front-runner sets the entire shape of this race from stall-rise; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that a truly dominant wire-to-wire display is not his mode, but in a small field where nobody presses him he can produce a very honest gallop — 72 days off is worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Eremenko shaped with promise when winning three starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going, while our rating of 109 makes her a leading threat; the main risk is a 72-day absence since her fourth-placed effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Roarin' Success
runners_data.note: Two wins from two at this trip on Good ground for the McCain second string, who is the natural travelling companion to Eremenko — if she jumps fluently and tracks the leader throughout, her recent form (5-1-1 last three) makes her the primary threat to her stablemate.|
runners_data.comment: Roarin' Success returns after 51 days off carrying a hefty 164 lb, and though she arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going before, she rates fifth of six on our figures and that weight burden makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Uhtred Ragnarson
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination but has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the rear of the field is congested with closers; his STYLE_FIT score (0.91) and form figures of 3-F-7-3-5 suggest he rarely wins these, and Tom Cannon will need a carbon-copy run to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Uhtred Ragnarson arrives here rated 110 by our assessors, topping the field of six, and his third two starts back hints at better to come; yet to score in his last five starts, and the 164 lb burden is the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride on this lightly weighted four-year-old who has winning form on Good ground at similar trips and was only last seen 17 days ago — the Skelton yard is in strong form (T14: 7/20) and Playful Fox's jumping ability at hurdle two from home is the main watch point in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Playful Fox arrives on the back of a win last time out, and was a winner three starts back too, with a runner-up effort sandwiched between; his trainer is in excellent nick at 35% over the past fortnight, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: John McConnell's five-year-old has been placed four times on Good and soft ground at this trip but has never won; naturally a hold-up horse, the redistribution note means Alex Harvey (3) is unlikely to get a clean passage from the back of a six-runner field, and the 0W4P similar-going record confirms the win potential is modest without a perfect scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Syosset faces a stiff ask under 156 lb, though he has shown consistent placed form recently and has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Eremenko is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners on Good ground at Bangor, he is likely to slot straight to the front and control a measured, sustainable gallop without any genuine challenger for the lead. Roarin' Success is the other prominent-type and will track Eremenko closely from the start, meaning the pace will be honest but not pressurised — a steady-to-fair tempo that keeps the field compact through the early stages. Hello Sweety and Playful Fox are genuine hold-up horses with the form to close from the rear, but a small field on Good ground rarely produces the gaps they need, and a prolonged controlled pace that quickens at the two-out flight tends to reward horses travelling well just off the speed. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset are true closers pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded, and neither is likely to get the clean, late run their natural style demands in this compressed, six-runner shape. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can sit within two lengths of Eremenko's controlled pace and produce a fluent jump two out will have first run on the closers — this race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-just-off-the-pace profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent pair control and kick
scenarios.trigger: If Eremenko leads at a steady-fair pace with Roarin' Success glued to his quarters and the race quickens from the second-last flight.
scenarios.body: Eremenko dictates every yard of a clean, unflustered race and the McCain duo fill the front two positions with no hold-up horse able to generate the momentum to close them down on Good ground; the compressed field and uncontested tempo mean the eventual winner arrives from within the front two.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse threads through
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes the field to concertina at the second-last, creating gaps for a closer to pick through late.
scenarios.body: Hello Sweety or Playful Fox, both with strong Good-ground form at this trip, get a clear run between tired rivals and finish with purpose; this shape requires a fractionally faster early pace than Eremenko is likely to set alone, so it is conditional on the McCain pair over-pressing each other.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sole front-runner bolts up
scenarios.trigger: If Eremenko's rivals misjudge their positions and he is allowed to slip the field at the top of the straight unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Roarin' Success is the most likely to deny this by tracking tightly, but if she misses a flight or loses contact, Eremenko's uncontested lead on Good ground becomes very difficult to reel in; his 1W2P record in similar going supports a front-running display if allowed to dictate fully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution chaos mid-race
scenarios.trigger: If Uhtred Ragnarson or Syosset work forward from their redistributed midfield position to press Eremenko, injecting a pace they are not naturally suited to sustain.
scenarios.body: A higher early tempo would shorten the race for true closers like Hello Sweety but would also expose Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset to a stamina test they create themselves; this scenario is assigned low probability precisely because both horses carry STYLE_FIT discounts and are unlikely to race genuinely forward in practice.

watchPoints.text: Roarin' Success jumps the second-last alongside Eremenko — whichever of the McCain pair is travelling better at that point will likely win, and Roarin' Success's sharp recent form makes her the danger to any other runner in the field.

Playful Fox's jumping has to be monitored: Harry Skelton will want to be tracking the leaders by the top of the straight, and any hesitation at the hurdles will cost her the position she needs to mount a late challenge.

Eremenko's 72-day absence is the primary fitness question — Donald McCain has had zero wins from three runners over 14 days (T14: 0/13), and if Eremenko shows any signs of ring-rustiness or makes a jumping error at the front, the race shape collapses entirely.

Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset are both true closers compressed into midfield on the map — if either drifts even further back than expected in running, watch for a late surge that flatters but ultimately falls short given the uncontested, controlled tempo ahead of them.

races.name: Bangor-on-dee Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hillview
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist for Gary Hanmer and Gavin Sheehan, running off a 51-day break; solid similar-going form (11/15) and course experience give him claims but he needs the pace to collapse in front of him, and at OR 100 he carries the joint-top weight.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a pulled-up effort 51 days ago warranting close scrutiny, Hillview nonetheless heads the ratings and carries today's trip and conditions on his CV, making him the one they all have to beat off 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Present Fair
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's nine-year-old hold-up type, course winner on Good over 2m3f (OR 98), back after 50 days with amateur Harry Brown (10lb claim) on board; the claim helps but he finished seventh over 2m2f last time and the amateur partnership over 2m7f is a consideration.|
runners_data.comment: Present Fair won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 105 suggesting he holds strong claims as the second-ranked runner here; the concern is a return from 50 days off and a hefty 166 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Camino Rocio
runners_data.note: Front-runner trained by Dan Skelton, ridden by Harry Skelton who brings a T14 rate of 7/20; racing just 16 days since last run, she has three wins and five places from 11 similar-going efforts and is the clear pace-controlling force in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Camino Rocio has finished second on three occasions in recent starts and has run over today's distance and going, with a trainer firing at 35% in the last fortnight; the pull-up last time out is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Scottish Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Tim Reed with a spotless 15/15 similar-going strike rate, showing wins at 1m6f and 2m on Good; stepping back to hurdles with a career-best placed run over 2m (OR 94) last time, though his hurdles form is over shorter distances than today's 2m7f trip, which is the key unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Scottish Dancer has gone without a win in his last five starts, yet his third last time out shows he retains ability, and he has experience of today's going; the main risk is the 83-day absence returning off a sizeable 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Seahouses
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from 142 days off for Barry Brennan, ridden by 5lb claimer Isabelle Ryder; limited Good-ground form (4/15) and a long lay-off make it hard to trust him to sustain his pace challenge for the full 2m7f trip, and Camino Rocio is likely to have his measure.|
runners_data.comment: Seahouses has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third three times in his last five starts, though a return after 142 days and a burden of 156 lb asks questions of a gelding yet to win in recent starts, despite having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style who sits mapped into midfield due to the congestion at the back of this field; he ran just 11 days ago and his recent form figures of 6P-04P show inconsistency, with the style displacement reducing his scope to operate from his preferred position.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and twice pulled up in recent outings, You Did faces stiff questions at 155 lb with a trainer firing at just 3% over the past fortnight, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick eleven-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: John McConnell's five-year-old carries headgear (tongue-tie and hood) and T14 form of 4/28; a natural hold-up performer whose last five runs over shorter hurdles trips (all 16-22f) make the step to 2m7f a significant stamina query, and he won't be racing from his most comfortable vantage point in this field shape.|
runners_data.comment: Fine Print has shown fleeting ability — third last time out — but winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, he carries 153 lb over a field that looks beyond him on current form.

runners_data.name: Fane Court
runners_data.note: Kielan Woods takes the ride for D J Jeffreys on this consistent prominent racer who has placed in his last three over 2m3-4f on Good or Heavy; OR 80 gives him a weight advantage and his placed-effort profile over similar trips makes him a live each-way candidate if he can track the leaders.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Fane Court has been out of action for 54 days and carries 148 lb, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Camino Rocio and Seahouses are the two confirmed front-runners here, and with Harry Skelton aboard the Skelton yard's Camino Rocio, that horse is likely to assert early and control the tempo at an honest, honest gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good ground. Seahouses has the pace to go with her but arrives on a 142-day break with a 5lb claimer, and Camino Rocio's record of consistent front-running makes her the more likely pace-setter to dictate terms from the front. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all settle in their natural positions — You Did and Fine Print are genuine hold-up horses who are effectively pushed into midfield positions because Hillview and Present Fair already occupy the rear, meaning neither will be racing from their most comfortable base. This contested but controlled pace over a stamina-testing trip will suit progressive prominent racers and horses with a strong staying profile, making the midfield-to-prominent travelling position the golden zone from which this race will be won.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camino Rocio Dictates Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Camino Rocio assumes full control at a fair pace and the hold-up brigade cannot close the gap late.
scenarios.body: Camino Rocio, with Harry Skelton steering and a T14 strike rate of 7/20, sets a measured honest gallop that suits her stamina profile, with rivals unable to mount a coordinated challenge over this stiff trip; her course-distance going profile (11/15 similar-going runs) underlines how effective she is in these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to set up a challenge for a prominent-travelling horse who can collar the leader from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Scottish Dancer, dropping back to hurdles from a chase background and showing a 15/15 similar-going record, is ideally placed to stalk the leaders and pounce; Fane Court's consistent placed form on similar going makes him the each-way danger from the same prominent berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Camino Rocio and Seahouses burn each other off with a faster-than-expected pace, leaving the race open for the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: Hillview (sim-going record 11/15, course experience) or Present Fair (a course winner at similar distances on Good) could pick off a weakening field in the straight; however, both You Did and Fine Print are natural hold-up types shuffled into midfield rather than their ideal deep position, reducing the potency of any late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If Seahouses refuses to commit and Camino Rocio eases up, creating a slow-run tactical race that turns into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a falsely-run race, shorter-trip performers such as Fine Print and You Did could find themselves ideally placed having been carried closer than ideal, though their redistribution out of natural hold-up roles means this is unlikely to play to their full strengths; Scottish Dancer's flat-race speed background could make him the beneficiary of any sprint to the line.

watchPoints.text: Seahouses — watch for him to jump and push for the lead from the front; if he and Camino Rocio set a strong pace together, the contest for supremacy between the two confirmed front-runners could burn them both off, transforming the finish entirely.

Scottish Dancer's stamina is unproven at 2m7f — watch how he travels into the back straight; if he struggles to hold his prominent position from the second circuit, his chance evaporates quickly over this trip.

You Did and Fine Print — both are genuine hold-up horses who cannot get to the back of the field in this shape; watch whether they over-race in midfield against their nature, which could drain their reserves before the final climb.

Fane Court's low weight of 148lbs and Kielan Woods' experience — watch whether he is allowed to creep into contention quietly in the final mile, as his placed form in similar conditions makes him a live danger at a big price if the race is run to suit.

Camino Rocio's jumping — she has a pulled-up run in her recent form and Bangor's tight bends demand slick hurdling; watch her over the early flights to see if she travels with her usual fluency before committing to her as the race-controlling force.
